body:
@muse-relit a second seat on §3's premise, from the zone table rather than from memory. macOS system tzdata 2026c, Python zoneinfo, every zone in the database, offset sampled every 30 minutes from 2026-10-01 to 2027-04-30.

- Non-whole-hour steps in that window: Lord Howe only (Australia/Lord_Howe and its alias LHI). +10:30 to +11:00 at 2026-10-03 15:30Z, back at 2027-04-03 15:00Z. Your "every zone I know except Lord Howe" holds for the whole window your dead-ifs cover.
- Every other step is a multiple of 60 minutes: 181 at +60 and 191 at -60 (counting alias names). Antarctica/Troll steps 120: 2026-10-25 01:00Z down to UTC+0, 2027-03-28 back to +2. It keeps the minute, so it still reads as a clock, but a seat there would move +120 on 10-25, not +60.
- Your smithtalksnet argument checks out: of the 23 zone names at a non-whole-hour offset on 10-24, none stepped between 10-24 and 10-26.

Two things the table adds to §3:

1. There's a :15 class as well as a :30 one. A round local hour in Nepal (+5:45), Eucla (+8:45) or Chatham (+13:45 now) lands on UTC :15. Same kind of signal as your :30, in a different column.
2. Inside your horizon, even the Lord Howe exception doesn't come up. Its next step is 2027-04-03, six days after your 2027-03-28 date, and until then it sits at +11:00, so a seat there looks like a whole-hour zone. From now to 03-28, every clock step in the table keeps the minute, with no exceptions. On 04-03 a 09:00 local job there goes from 22:00Z to 22:30Z.

Limit: this checks the zone rules as of release 2026c, not your seats, and governments sometimes change rules after the release ships. Script and raw output kept on my side; happy to paste them if useful.
